results.title: [PDF] Knowledge Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation via GNN ...
results.content: Extensive experiments on Question-Answering tasks demonstrate that our method significantly improves retrieval accuracy and answer quality, demonstrating the effec-tiveness of combining graph-based reasoning and LLM-driven retrieval for structured knowledge integration.1 1 Introduction Large Language Models (LLMs) (Brown et al., 2020; Touvron et al., 2023) have achieved remarkable success in natural language processing (NLP) tasks, including text compre-hension (Lewis et al., 2020a), language generation (Cheng et al., 2023), and open-domain question answering (QA) (Wei et al., 2022; Cohen et al., 2024; Chen et al., 2024). The framework consists of: (1) Subgraph Extraction, where contextualized subgraphs are extracted from the KG based on entities mentioned in the question; (2) Question-Relevance Scoring, where we calculate question-relevance scores based on a trainable graph neural network and a fixed LM encoder; (3) LLM Stepwise Retrieval, where relation and entity candidates are filtered from the GNN scores and the LLM retrieves relevant knowledge paths guided by GNN scores and semantic similarity scores; the selected knowledge triplets are then used to construct prompts.

Title: Understanding Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and Best Practices | by Superbo AI Hub | Medium
# Understanding Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and Best Practices. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) is a key technique in modern LLM-based applications, wherein a dedicated retrieval module extracts relevant, up-to-date, or domain-specific information that is then incorporated into the LLM’s prompt. Many IT teams believe that building their own RAG system is a simple case of **loading documents in any solution and running similarity searches**. * Product catalog or Troubleshooting RAGs are examples where simple embeddings-based retrieval methods may fall short in capturing the structured relationships or precise information in these domains. The same logic applies to **RAG** — a production-grade system **requires deep engineering expertise, security controls, and a scalable architecture** that most IT teams underestimate. One of the biggest misunderstandings is treating **RAG as just “a knowledge base with search.”** This **reduces RAG to an outdated model** when, in reality, it is a **dynamic and evolving framework**. * Unlike KBs, RAG dynamically retrieves **contextual and time-sensitive data** rather than relying on a **pre-built** dataset. * Search engines return **ranked lists of results**, whereas RAG **extracts, synthesizes, and augments responses** before sending them to an LLM. * RAG is an **adaptive system**, integrating **multi-step retrieval pipelines, vector indexing, and API access** for enhanced knowledge augmentation. Not all RAG implementations are equal — some require **simple retrieval**, while others demand **complex multi-step reasoning**. 1. **Explicit Fact Queries:** Simple lookup-based retrieval (e.g., *“What is the GDP of France?”*). Advanced RAG systems leverage **multi-turn reasoning** and **AI agents** to handle complex **research, legal analysis, and predictive decision-making**. * Implement **metadata-based retrieval**, **semantic vector search**, and **re-ranking models**. * **Next-gen RAG systems** leverage **AI agents** for: **Multi-source synthesis, long-form reasoning, automating multi-step research**. RAG is a **powerful tool** for enterprise AI, but **building it in-house** is often a **costly and inefficient mistake**. **Superbo’s RAGulous** delivers **enterprise-grade** RAG with **built-in LLM security, retrieval pipelines, scalable indexing from unstructured or structured data sources, and AI-driven ranking models** — eliminating the risks of **DIY solutions** while ensuring **high-accuracy, secure, and cost-effective knowledge augmentation**. ### Architectures beyond Naive Rag to build reliable production AI Systems. ### PageIndex is a vectorless, reasoning-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) approach that retrieves answers from long documents without….

results.title: Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)
results.content: Published Time: 2024-07-05 Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) * Prompt Engineering 101 - Beginner's Guide * Prompt Engineering Techniques - Intermediate Guide (Reasoning) * Using Vector Embeddings for AI products * Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) * Building AI Products using Large Language Models (LLMs) Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) July 5, 2024 - 10 min read > Note: This article is a summary of a paper on "Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation" by Wang et al. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) techniques combine the strengths of pretraining and retrieval-based models to mitigate these issues, enhancing model performance. Previous research has explored methods to enhance query information through transformation techniques, thereby improving retrieval performance. * Query2Doc and HyDE generate pseudo-documents from original queries to enhance retrieval accuracy. ### Retriever Enhancement Strategy The methods used for document chunking and embedding significantly impact retrieval performance. ### Retriever and Generator Fine-tuning Fine-tuning both retrievers and generators within the RAG framework is crucial for optimizing performance. Holistic approaches treat RAG as an integrated system, fine-tuning both retriever and generator together to enhance overall performance, despite the increased complexity and integration challenges. ### Query Classification Not all queries require retrieval-augmented responses due to the inherent capabilities of LLMs. While RAG can enhance information accuracy and reduce hallucinations, frequent retrieval can increase response time. ### Vector Databases Vector databases store embedding vectors with their metadata, enabling efficient retrieval of documents relevant to queries through various indexing and approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) methods. ### Retrieval Methods Given a user query, the retrieval module selects the top-k relevant documents from a pre-built corpus based on the similarity between the query and the documents. ### Reranking Methods After the initial retrieval, a reranking phase is employed to enhance the relevance of the retrieved documents, ensuring that the most pertinent information appears at the top of the list. Therefore, efficient methods to summarize retrieved documents are crucial in the RAG pipeline. This study aims to identify optimal practices for implementing retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) to improve the quality and reliability of content produced by large language models. * Retriever and Generator Fine-tuning * Searching for Best RAG Practices * Best Practices for Implementing RAG
